item.title: Grammys Chief Responds to BTS’ Decision To Not Enter Its Songs for Consideration at 2027 Grammys
item.description:
Here's a short, engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome back to "Music News"! Today, we're talking about the Grammys and a big decision made by K-pop supergroup BTS. The group has announced that they will not be submitting their music for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards.
[Short music transition]
Host: According to a statement posted on their Instagram accounts, the seven members of BTS said, "We have decided not to submit to the Grammys this year. We hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language." This move seems to be in response to the Recording Academy's newly created Best Asian Pop Music Performance category.
[Short music transition]
Host: In response to BTS' decision, Grammys CEO Harvey Mason Jr. released a statement saying that the Asian Pop category was created to celebrate the diversity and growth of pop artistry coming out of Asia. He emphasized that submitting music in a genre category doesn't exclude an artist from also submitting in the General Field categories, such as Record of the Year or Album of the Year.
[Short music transition]
Host: It's worth noting that both Harvey Mason Jr. and BTS have something in common - they've both received exactly five Grammy nominations without winning. Mason as a producer and songwriter, and BTS as a group.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in to "Music News"! We'll be keeping an eye on this story and bringing you more updates as they come. Don't forget to subscribe to our podcast for more music news and discussions. See you next time!
